sessionTitle: Local models, developer control, and the future of AI runtimes

announcements.name: Ollama Launch
announcements.shortDescription: A command that injects open models directly into existing tools such as Claude Code [inferred], VS Code, and GitHub Copilot, with one-line setup for agent harnesses.
announcements.longDescription: Ollama Launch is a recently introduced command that integrates open models directly with a developer's favorite tools. By using the command, open models can be injected directly into harnesses such as Claude Code [inferred], VS Code, and GitHub Copilot. It builds on Ollama's core proposition of being the easiest way for developers to access and run open models in one command.

announcements.name: Ollama Cloud
announcements.shortDescription: An optional service introduced this year that runs frontier-grade open models on data-center hardware with zero data retention and no training on user data, for users lacking local compute.
announcements.longDescription: Ollama Cloud was added starting this year to augment local inference, allowing users to run frontier models on data-center-grade hardware when they lack sufficient local compute. Data is never trained on and the service has zero data retention. It enables use cases such as parallel agents to accomplish difficult work not possible with smaller models, with models offering the maximum context window from the providers themselves. It is a completely optional service usable with Ollama.

announcements.name: MLX inference engine
announcements.shortDescription: A native Apple-device inference path (supporting NVFP4) offering faster performance than the previous engine when pulling MLX models from Ollama's registry.
announcements.longDescription: In response to a question about whether Ollama still uses llama.cpp under the hood and plans for its own engine, the speaker noted Ollama has its own MLX inference engine. For users on an Apple device, it is highly recommended because it offers faster performance. To use it, you just need to pull one of the MLX models from Ollama's model registry.

announcements.name: OpenAI and Anthropic API compatibility
announcements.shortDescription: Compatibility plus Python and JavaScript SDKs for developers building applications on open models.
announcements.longDescription: For developers building applications on top of open models, Ollama provides OpenAI and Anthropic API compatibility. Developers with Python or JavaScript applications also have an SDK to build on top of. Ollama has been built for agents from the beginning, with specific testing for tool calling, structured outputs, and one-line agent setup.
